items.title: Model income, detect payroll expectations and build the variable-income budgeting engine
items.outcome: As a user, the application knows what I expect to earn and when, notices when my salary is late or short, handles irregular income properly, and produces budgets that still work when my income is not the same every month.
items.context: A payoff plan that ignores income is guesswork, and variable income is the case most budgeting products handle badly. Getting it right is a differentiator; getting it wrong makes the product useless to freelancers and to anyone paid irregularly.
scope: Salary configuration with amount, frequency and next expected date
Expected versus received detection across the transaction stream
Additional and irregular income typed and excluded correctly from fixed budgets
Budgeting engine that works from a distribution rather than a fixed monthly figure
Category budgets with rollover across period boundaries
acceptance_criteria: A late or short salary is surfaced with the expectation it was measured against
The detector's false positive rate is measured on a synthetic corpus and recorded
Budgets produce correct results for weekly, fortnightly, monthly and irregular income, proven by property tests
Rollover arithmetic is exact across month boundaries including short and long months
All arithmetic agrees with the independent model across the case matrix
Income records use the published money representation with no floating point anywhere
contracts_schema: Implements the published income and budget contract
security_privacy: Salary amount is treated as sensitive descriptive data under the encryption decision
Detection never sends income data outside the system
observability: Publishes detection counts and budget computation latency without amounts
tests: Detector false positive measurement on a synthetic corpus
rollout_rollback: Behind a flag; the detector ships in observe-only mode first so false positives do not alarm users
Rollback disables detection while budgets remain functional
non_goals: Tax computation and investment tracking
Any recommendation to buy a financial product

items.title: Compute safe-to-spend, cash-flow forecast and the surplus feed to the debt simulator
items.outcome: As a user, I can see what I can safely spend today, what my next ninety days look like, and how much spare money I could put toward my debt this month, with every figure reconciling exactly against my ledger.
items.context: Safe-to-spend is the number people act on, so it has to reconcile exactly or it becomes a reason to distrust everything else. Feeding surplus into the debt simulator is what closes the loop between budgeting and the product wedge.
scope: Safe-to-spend computed from income less committed outflows, debt payments and goal contributions
Derivation exposed so a client can show how the figure was reached
Thirty, sixty and ninety day cash-flow forecast computed deterministically
Bill and subscription calendar with due dates feeding the forecast
Surplus detection offered to the debt simulator as a suggested extra payment
Budget threshold and overspend messages are enqueued through the T-NOT-01 outbox; this ticket sends nothing directly and adds no delivery mechanism
acceptance_criteria: Safe-to-spend reconciles exactly against the ledger; a discrepancy fails the test rather than being rounded away
The derivation lists every input so a client renders it without recomputing
The forecast is deterministic and is validated against a subsequent real month on synthetic data
No forecast figure is produced by a model; all arithmetic is deterministic
A suggested extra payment never exceeds the computed surplus
All figures agree with the independent model
contracts_schema: Implements the published safe-to-spend, forecast and surplus contract including derivation fields
security_privacy: Reminder payloads carry no monetary values
Forecast outputs are scoped to the requesting user only
observability: Publishes computation latency and reconciliation mismatch counts, alerting on any mismatch
rollout_rollback: Behind a flag per surface so the forecast can be withdrawn without removing safe-to-spend
Rollback hides the figure rather than showing a stale one
non_goals: Model-generated projections of any kind
Notification delivery, scheduling, preferences and provider integration, which T-NOT-01 owns

items.title: Build the goal engine with projections, multi-goal competition and income-gap analysis
items.outcome: As a user, I can set long-horizon goals, see honestly whether I am on track, and see exactly how funding one goal delays another, all computed deterministically from my own data.
items.context: Once the payoff date is known, the same deterministic machinery answers what comes next. The differentiating and honest feature is showing the trade-off between goals rather than pretending they are independent, and the regulatory line is that this remains a calculator rather than an adviser.
scope: Goal model with target amount, target date, priority and linked accounts
Goal types covering debt-free, purchase, emergency fund and custom
Required savings rate and projected completion computed deterministically
Multi-goal competition showing the exact delay one goal imposes on another
Income-gap analysis computed only from the user's own data
Scenario comparison presented as options rather than instructions
Goal milestone and off-track messages are enqueued through the T-NOT-01 outbox; this ticket sends nothing directly and adds no delivery mechanism
acceptance_criteria: Projections are deterministic and agree with the independent model across the case matrix
Funding one goal shows the exact delay to each other goal, with the derivation inspectable
Income-gap analysis uses no external benchmark in the computation path
No projection is produced by a model; the engine is the only source
An unreachable goal produces an explicit result stating the shortfall rather than an optimistic date
Every projection response carries the disclaimer version identifier the client must render
contracts_schema: Implements the published goal contract including competition and derivation fields
security_privacy: Goal data is scoped to the owner; shared household goals go through the sharing authorization model
No output names a financial product or a specific security
observability: Publishes projection computation counts and latency without amounts
tests: Copy scan for advice-boundary terms in generated text
rollout_rollback: Behind a flag; projections ship after the independent model comparison is green
Rollback hides projections while stored goals remain intact

Any lending or brokering activity, permanently

items.title: Compute personal net worth and its trend from the ledger with per-currency separation
items.outcome: As a user, my net worth and its trend are computed deterministically from my own ledger, held as one bucket per currency rather than combined into a single false total, with the full derivation exposed and an explicit incomplete-data state whenever a linked account's balance is missing or stale.
items.context: Net worth is the first cross-account rollup the product ships, and the most common way to get it wrong is to add balances in different currencies into one friendlier-looking number. The ledger and money-format decision records both require that a mixed-currency total never be produced silently, so this ticket returns a snapshot and trend per currency; combining currencies into one total stays out of scope until the globalization epic delivers a conversion path.
scope: Net-worth snapshot computed as assets minus liabilities, held as a separate bucket per currency
Historical trend series derived from ledger snapshots at a defined cadence
Derivation listing every account and balance that contributed to a bucket
Explicit incomplete-data state when an account's balance is stale or unavailable, rather than silently omitting it
No currency conversion or combined cross-currency total anywhere in the computation path
acceptance_criteria: A user with accounts in two currencies never receives a single combined total, proven by a test asserting one bucket per currency
The trend series reconciles exactly against the ledger snapshots it was derived from
An account with a stale or missing balance produces the explicit incomplete-data state rather than being silently excluded
The derivation lists every contributing account and balance so a client can render it without recomputing
All figures agree with the independent model across the case matrix, and no floating point value appears anywhere in the response
contracts_schema: Implements the published net-worth contract from T-CON-08 including its per-currency bucket and derivation shapes
security_privacy: Net-worth figures are scoped to the requesting user only and reuse the encryption and access rules already established for account balances
observability: Publishes computation latency and reconciliation mismatch counts, alerting on any mismatch
rollout_rollback: Behind a flag per surface so the figure can be withdrawn without removing the underlying accounts
Rollback hides the figure rather than showing a stale one
non_goals: Currency conversion and any combined cross-currency total, which stays out of scope until the globalization epic (E30) delivers a conversion path
Any forecast or projection of future net worth
items.parallel_boundary: Primary repo api. Owns the net-worth computation module. Clients render the per-currency derivation rather than recomputing or converting it.

items.title: Build Android category spending, budgets and reporting parity
items.outcome: An Android user can see where money went by category and period, set and track budgets, and read the same income, budget and net worth figures the web product shows, so the primary client is not the one with the least reporting.
items.context: Income, budgeting, goals and net worth all gained web surfaces and server implementations, and Android - the primary client and the only one with capture - received none of them. That leaves the product in the position of collecting a user's data on the phone and requiring a browser to understand it. Parity here is not a nice-to-have: the categorisation work is only worth anything if the user can see its output where they already are.
scope: Category spending by period with drill-down into the transactions behind a figure
Budget creation, editing and progress against the server-computed budget state
Income summary and recurring-income presentation consistent with the server model
Net worth presentation reading the same derived values as the web surface
Period selection, comparison against the previous period, and the rule for an incomplete current period
Offline and stale behaviour: what a report shows when it cannot refresh, using the T-UX-01 taxonomy
Empty and low-data states that explain what is missing rather than showing an empty chart
acceptance_criteria: Category totals, budget progress, income and net worth figures match the server-computed values exactly for the same period, asserted by a test rather than by inspection
Every figure is derived from the canonical money representation and is never re-parsed from a formatted string
Drilling into a category total lists exactly the transactions that compose it, and their sum equals the total
An incomplete current period is labelled as incomplete and is never compared against a complete previous period without saying so
A stale report is labelled stale and offline is distinguished from stale exactly as T-UX-01 defines
Empty and low-data states explain what is required to produce a figure rather than rendering a zeroed chart
The screens pass the accessibility and performance budgets applied to the other core journeys, including chart alternatives for screen readers
contracts_schema: Consumes the published income, budget, category and net worth contracts through the generated client; no aggregate is recomputed locally except for offline presentation of already-fetched data
security_privacy: Reports are rendered from data the client already holds or is entitled to fetch; no new server capability is introduced
Screenshots of report surfaces are subject to the same protections as the rest of the financial UI
observability: Report open rates, period selections and drill-down rates are recorded so an unused report is visible before it is expanded
tests: Server-agreement test for category, budget, income and net worth figures
rollout_rollback: Ships one report at a time behind flags, starting with category spending which has the most existing data behind it
Rollback hides the surfaces; no local schema or server contract changes are required to remove them
non_goals: Server-side budgeting, income and net worth computation, which T-INC-01, T-INC-02 and T-NWT-01 own
Goal planning surfaces, which T-GOL-02 owns
Export, which the trust and compliance tickets own
